title: to_cents rounds half-even, not half-up
explanation: quantize() without a rounding argument uses the context default ROUND_HALF_EVEN, so 2.345 becomes 2.34 instead of 2.35, contradicting the docstring and README. Every payroll amount is affected. Pass rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP.

title: Prorate arguments swapped for salaried new joiners
explanation: prorate(employee.rate, days_in_month, worked) computes salary * days_in_month / worked instead of salary * worked / days_in_month. Someone joining on 16 April with a 3000 salary is paid 6000 instead of 1500; the more days missed, the more they are paid.

title: Department totals are not reset between departments
explanation: When the department changes only headcount is reset (line 46); gross, deductions and net keep accumulating, so every department after the first includes the money of all previous departments, contrary to the docstring.

title: SQL injection in by_department
explanation: The department typed in by HR on the web form is interpolated into the SQL string. A value like x' OR '1'='1 returns every employee and other payloads can read arbitrary data; a quote in a legitimate department name breaks the query. Use a ? parameter.

title: Timesheet period is not checked against the payslip period
explanation: build_payslip only checks the employee id. A March timesheet passed for an April payslip is silently paid as April hours. Check timesheet.year/month equal year/month.

title: Overtime lost for ISO weeks spanning two months
explanation: A timesheet only holds the days of one month, so a week that straddles a month boundary is split in two and each part is compared to 40 hours separately. 30 h at the end of March plus 20 h at the start of April (50 h in one ISO week) produces no overtime at all, violating the 'above 40 hours in an ISO week' rule.

title: Flat health insurance can make net pay negative
explanation: Health insurance of 25.00 is charged whenever gross > 0. An employee whose gross is below the deductions (e.g. one hour worked) gets a negative net, which then goes into the bank transfer file as a negative payment. Cap deductions at gross or carry the shortfall.

title: parse_amount raises InvalidOperation and accepts NaN/Infinity
explanation: Invalid text such as 'abc' raises decimal.InvalidOperation, not ValueError, so callers handling the documented ValueError miss it. 'NaN' parses and returns NaN; 'Infinity' raises from quantize. Commas are stripped anywhere ('1,2,3' -> 123). Validate the format and finiteness.

title: Overtime rule duplicated in the report module
explanation: overtime_by_department re-implements split_overtime with its own WEEKLY_HOURS constant (line 17) instead of reusing timesheets.split_overtime/OVERTIME_THRESHOLD, so the two can drift apart. It also raises KeyError for a timesheet whose employee is not in the list.

title: Payslip rendering duplicated
explanation: _payslip_block is a copy of Payslip.render_text; any change to the payslip layout must be made twice. Reuse render_text.

title: Connection lifetime not managed
explanation: EmployeeStore opens a SQLite connection in __init__ but offers no context-manager support; any exception between creation and close() leaks the connection.
